invariants.rationale: The method always returns a new Value instance, which cannot be null.
There is an explicit null check and exception thrown if actor is null before returning, so actor is always non-null at exit.
This expresses that percent is always a float (i.e., not NaN). If percent was NaN, both comparisons would be false. This can help assert percent is a valid float value.
The result is always an instance of an anonymous subclass of Value.
Per implementation, the Value object returned always computes actor.getHeight() multiplied by percent for its get method.
